h: A cursed ring and a link to Tolkien
p: One of The Vyne's most unusual treasures is a Roman gold ring found in a field in Hampshire in the 18th century. It is linked to a curse tablet discovered at a Roman site in Gloucestershire, where a man named Silvianus asked the gods to punish whoever had stolen his ring. In the 1920s, the archaeologists studying the curse consulted a young academic named J.R.R. Tolkien, and many people believe the story helped inspire the One Ring. The ring is displayed at The Vyne, and it is a must-see for any Lord of the Rings fan.

The Chute family owned the house for centuries, and their portraits and possessions give the place a friendly, lived-in feel. The Tudor chapel's stained glass is worth seeing in good light, when the colours really glow.
Allow half a day for the house, gardens and a walk. The lake and wetland areas are good for birdwatching, so bring binoculars if you have them.

Nearby, Basing House in Old Basing tells the story of one of the longest sieges of the English Civil War, and Milestones Museum in Basingstoke recreates streets from Victorian times to the mid-20th century. Jane Austen fans will know she was born in the village of Steventon near Basingstoke, and her later home at Chawton is a short drive away.
